Subject: Token-path mapping reconciliation + owner matrix for Console telemetry

Hi team / Sarah —

We noticed a gap between the Console "Tenant token spend" tile and Nimbus's billing export for the week of Oct 3–9. The tile shows ~18% higher token cost for their production route than the billing CSV. Sarah, thank you for sending the export offline — attaching the extract Nimbus pulled (nimbus_console_tile_extract_oct2026.csv).

Quick ask: we need to reconcile where the token-to-cost mapping is diverging (token classification, sub-route mapping, or attribution) and land on a short owner matrix so Nimbus has a single point of contact for follow-ups. Proposed immediate checklist: 
- Compare token counts by route + model variant (Console) vs Nimbus billing rows (they export per-api-key).
- Validate any sampling/aggregation windows (we suspect our sampling at higher percentiles hid some long sequences).
- Confirm whether prefix/KV cache savings were applied to their tenant billing.

Jasmine / Soojin — can you lead the technical diff (what telemetry shows vs raw token logs)?
Kimberly — can you own billing-side reconciliation (how we map Console routes to customer ledger rows)?
Irene — can you coordinate the owner matrix doc and updates to the Console tile note explaining known caveats?

Timeline: aiming for a short internal reconciliation + proposed owner matrix by EOD Thu (2026-10-15). If we need Nimbus validation earlier, Sarah is available for a 30m sync on Thu morning (she said morning PT works).

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T14:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Token-path mapping reconciliation + owner matrix for Console telemetry

Marcus / team — I've started a quick diff between the Console tile ingestion and the raw token logs. Early findings: 
1) Sampling and aggregation: Console's tenant tile samples at 5% to keep dashboard latency low. For high-tail sequences (>1k tokens) the sampling bias can undercount overall token volume because we drop rare long sessions and extrapolate incorrectly. That would cause Console to show lower tokens, not higher — so this doesn't explain Nimbus seeing fewer ledger tokens.
2) Attribution mismatch: Our tile groups by "route_path" which is derived from the public route name; Nimbus's billing groups by api_key. There are two internal route aliases ("/v1/chat/prod" and "/v1/chat/prod-legacy") that both map to the same api_key for Nimbus; however an internal router rewrite means some requests land with a normalized route (we'll show the list). That could double-count on our side if dedup logic isn't applied consistently.
3) KV cache accounting: I see that cache-hit adjustments are applied in a downstream multiplier but the Console pre-aggregation step currently reports raw tokens before cache deductions (we note cache savings separately). Nimbus billing reduces billed tokens for cache hits, so if Console displays pre-deduction tokens that could be the reason their billed rows are lower.

Next steps I propose: 
- I will export a route->api_key mapping for the Oct 3–9 window and produce a reconciled token count (raw vs post-cache) by Oct 14 COB.
- Soojin, can you validate the sampling extrapolation math and add a short note in the Console tile tooltip doc?
- Kimberly, we'll need the ledger mapping logic from you so we apply the same api_key grouping.

I linked a draft owner matrix and the alignment doc here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e-owner-matrix (owner-matrix-draft.xlsx).

Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Data Engineer, Inference Observability
